correctness.rationale: The exact Dirichlet coefficient matrix, all four zero-index cases, and the beta bound yield Hilbert–Schmidt compactness. The normalized log-coordinate kernels converge in L2 by a uniform e^{-max(x,y)} bound; the zero-index contribution is o(1) after epsilon scaling. The limiting Volterra T*T kernel gives a Bessel ODE and its positive J0 roots by the L2-at-infinity and derivative-at-zero conditions. The singular values and HS norm follow from Hilbert–Schmidt convergence. A finite diagnostic checker passed 54 assertions; no finite experiment was used as proof.

value.rationale: This canonical beta perturbation approaches the genuinely unbounded Lebesgue-moment operator on classical Dirichlet space. The result determines a full infinite family of leading approximation-number constants, not merely compactness or boundedness, as well as the sharp HS norm. Bessel zeros arise from a structural weighted-Volterra limit and provide a useful model for spectral phase transitions.
